matches.gold_text: Proposals must be emailed to the Research Director at MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 10 a.m. Central on the due date, August 21, 2024, according to the email time stamp.
The submittal must include a project plan, the proposed project team and its background, and any related projects now active or recently completed by the firm.
Questions and comments about the RFP must be sent to the Research Director by email by the deadline of 7/17/2024, 4 p.m. Central.
The proposal must include all data required in the Required Elements of Proposal section, or it may be disqualified.
The proposal should reference the project number and title, since more than one RFP may be due at the same time.
The Work Plan section of the proposal should be no longer than ten pages and use a font size of at least 12 points, excluding forms and resumes.
The project plan must include all items outlined in Section 2 (Scope of Work).
The project plan must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve the work plans.
Proposals must include a work plan with a proposed timeline.
The Personnel section should give the name, location, telephone number and email address of the Offeror's primary contact person.
The Offeror must provide a complete listing of each sub-offeror, if any, with complete contact information.
The proposal must clearly identify the Offeror's experience in offering the requested services during the past three years.
Proposals should give the name, title and telephone number of at least three client officials from within the past three years as references.
The proposal must be submitted as a single combined PDF document.

The proposal must contain only the required documents, in this order: Proposal Submission Form, Cover Letter, Body of Proposal (including work plan and project schedule), Personnel, Organization's Project Experience, Team Member Experience, and Organization's Client References.
A cover letter is optional and, if included, must not exceed one page.
The Offeror must submit a proposed cost estimate covering all services defined in the Scope of Work.
The cost estimate must be shown on the Section (4) Price Page, which must be completed, signed and returned with the proposal.
The services must be provided for a price not exceeding $175,000.
The contract period will be 15 months.
The Offeror must submit quarterly updates on work accomplished on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December throughout the project.
The quarterly updates must be submitted electronically to the MoDOT project manager.
An interim presentation to update MoDOT on progress must be completed by 9/15/2025.
The Offeror must provide ongoing progress updates by email and phone to MoDOT contacts every month.
The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025.
The final report, summary report, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026, about one month before the contract ends.
The final invoice is due and the contract ends on 2/2/2026.
The Offeror must facilitate a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to establish a protocol for regular communications and coordination.
The Offeror must schedule and conduct quarterly project status meetings reviewing past progress and upcoming work, in person or online.
The Offeror must develop minutes for the kick-off meeting and each quarterly status meeting.
The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan to MoDOT within two weeks after the project kick-off meeting.
The Data Management Plan should address use of platform-independent, non-proprietary data formats to maximize future utility of the data.
The Offeror must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
Before work begins on the proof of concept, the Offeror must provide the name of the program used to develop the legal land descriptions.
MoDOT Information Systems must approve the program before the Offeror proceeds to Task 3c (proof of concept).
The Offeror must demonstrate that the technology can create draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties.
The Offeror must provide training to MoDOT right-of-way staff once the system is developed and finalized.
The training must come with a user manual for staff to reference.
The Offeror must prepare a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study.
The draft documents should be final products apart from revisions based on MoDOT's review.
The final report must include a completed Technical Report Documentation page.
The Offeror must develop a final report detailing the tasks completed and all findings from the project.
The Offeror must provide a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions.
The Offeror must provide a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing important details of the project.
Property descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide.
Property rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described using the metes and bounds method unless the property is acquired in its entirety.
When a property is acquired in its entirety, the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Offerors are encouraged to obtain 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation.
All documents and reports produced by the Offeror at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC's property.
MHTC may reproduce and use any products derived from the Offeror's work without paying royalties or fees.
The Offeror should be able to provide certificates of general liability insurance of at least $500,000 per person per occurrence and $3,000,000 per occurrence overall.
The Offeror should be able to provide certificates of automobile liability insurance of at least $500,000 per person per occurrence and $3,000,000 per occurrence overall.
The Offeror should be able to provide a Missouri workers' compensation policy or equivalent as required by state law.
All applications must be developed with an approved runtime: a currently supported .NET 6.0 or later release, or .NET Framework 4.8 or later only where specifically needed.
Web applications must use the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework.
Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior approval from the IS Best Practices Review Team and IS management.
Large-scale use of Python requires approval of the IS Best Practices Review Team.
Customer applications should be web-based, browser applications.
Applications should be tested and designed for the latest IS-approved browsers at a minimum.
No client-side software other than a modern browser should be required to run the web application.
On-premise database deployments must run on Oracle 19C or on the latest supported SQL Server (SQL Server 2016 or higher only if approved by MoDOT IS).
No personally identifiable information may be stored in any database table unless the application has a specific business need for it.
Any stored PII must be approved by the IS Cyber Security Team.
All web applications must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
Content from another author's web pages must not be used unless the author explicitly allows free copying or arrangements are made with the author.
The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft legal land descriptions by 4/25/2025.
After adjusting the tool, the Offeror must create a manual and train ROW staff by 7/25/2025.
New development should use the approved programming languages: C#, JavaScript, CSS and HTML (Python only for limited uses).
All web applications must meet the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, based on Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.
Vendor logos, branding or endorsements must not appear in the application where a supported, licensed option exists to remove them.
Library dependencies used in the application should be reviewed and updated annually.

verdicts.text: Proposals for project TR202504, "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central.
Proposals must be submitted by qualified organizations, namely private consultants, universities, and research organizations.
Proposals must be submitted within the RFP's stated submission deadlines, as time is of the essence.
The Offeror must agree to provide the services at the fees quoted, under the terms of this RFP.
The proposal must be signed by an authorized signatory of the Offeror and dated.
The proposal must include the Offeror's printed or typed name, mailing address, city, state, zip, telephone, fax and electronic mail address.
The bidder must be a qualified organization that conducts the TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions" study for the MHTC and Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT).
Property descriptions prepared on behalf of the MHTC must be prepared in a manner that meets the requirements outlined in the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2.
Realty rights acquired or conveyed by the MHTC must be described using the metes and bounds method, unless the property is acquired in its entirety.
When a property is acquired in its entirety, the property description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record for the subject property.
The AI/ML solution must produce a "first draft" of the legal land description (LLD) using the MHTC parameters, which MoDOT's Right of Way staff can then review and edit.
The contract period will run for 15 months.
All RFP events must occur between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central time.

Email to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov is the only acceptable method of contact regarding the RFP, and contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and cause for disqualification, including all requests for information, data and manuals.
Questions or comments must be submitted no later than 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central.
A proposal is not considered submitted until the submitter receives notification of receipt from MoDOT.
The Offeror must deliver a final report, summary, presentation, and user manual.
Proposals must include a work plan with a proposed timeline.
Quarterly updates on work accomplished during the quarter must be submitted on or before the last working day of March, June, September, and December for the duration of the project.
Quarterly updates must be submitted electronically to the MoDOT project manager.
An interim presentation must be scheduled near the mid-point of the project to update MoDOT on progress and project direction.
E-mail and phone communications with MoDOT contacts are required on a monthly basis to provide ongoing updates of progress.
The Offeror must present on 4/25/2025 how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs.
The draft final report, summary report, and user manual are due on 11/3/2025.
The final invoice is due and the contract ends on 2/2/2026.
The successful Offeror shall provide the services described in the RFP for a total not to exceed $175,000.
The Offeror must provide Construction and Materials with an electronic copy of a program proposal that will help bring the project to successful completion.
The Offeror must facilitate a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to establish a protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination with the team.
The Offeror must schedule and conduct quarterly project status meetings reviewing progress for the previous period and anticipated work for the next period.
The Offeror must develop minutes for the kick-off meeting and for each quarterly status meeting.
The finalized work plan must detail implementation of the project tasks as well as the resources and schedule required to carry them out.
The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan (DMP) to MoDOT within 2 weeks after the project kick-off meeting.
The Data Management Plan must describe the anticipated format(s) the Offeror's data and related files will use.
The Data Management Plan should address how the Offeror will use platform-independent and non-proprietary formats to ensure maximum future utility of the data.
The vendor must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way (ROW) purposes.
Before work begins on the proof of concepts, the Offeror must provide the name of the program used to develop the LLDs.
MoDOT Information Systems must approve the named LLD development program before the Offeror may move forward with Task 3c.
The Offeror must demonstrate how its technology will create draft legal land descriptions for a variety of properties.
Once the system has been developed and finalized, the Offeror must provide training to ROW staff.

The Offeror must develop a final report detailing the tasks completed during the project, including all findings generated during the project's duration.
The Offeror must provide a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions.

Offerors are encouraged to submit copies of their existing affirmative action programs, if any.

The Offeror remains ultimately responsible and liable to MHTC for the complete, accurate and professional quality and performance of the services regardless of any subcontractors or suppliers used.
The Offeror shall comply with all provisions of Missouri Executive Order 07-13 (issued March 6, 2007) regarding not employing individuals who are not eligible to work in the United States.

Each sole proprietor and general partner of a sole proprietorship or partnership must submit a sworn affidavit of lawful presence using the form attached as Exhibit B.

All documents, reports, exhibits and other deliverables produced by the Offeror at the direction of MHTC's representative, along with information supplied by MHTC's representative, shall remain the property of MHTC.
The Offeror shall not disclose confidential factual matters provided to it to third parties except as required by statute, ordinance, or court order, or as authorized by MHTC's representative.
The Offeror shall notify MHTC immediately of any request for such confidential information.
The Offeror must maintain all working papers and records relating to the Agreement.

Automobile Liability insurance must be not less than $500,000 for any one person in a single accident or occurrence and not less than $3,000,000 for all claims arising out of a single occurrence.
The Offeror must maintain a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent in accordance with state law.
All applications must be developed using one of the technologies approved in the Approved Technologies section of the RFP.
A currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release should be used unless there is a specific need for .NET Framework.
If .NET Framework is required, a currently supported 4.8 release or above must be used.
Web applications must use either the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework.
Library dependencies used in the application should be reviewed and updated on an annual basis.

Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management.
New development should use only the approved programming languages: C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python.
Python is reserved for ESRI scripts and other small one-time uses, and large-scale use of Python requires approval of the Information Systems (IS) Best Practices Review Team (BRPT).
For platforms other than ArcGIS Desktop, ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Enterprise, version 3.x of Python from www.python.org should be used.
All customer applications should be web-based browser applications.
Applications should be tested and designed to use the latest IS-approved browser(s) at a minimum.
No client-side software other than a modern browser (e.g., no Java Applets, no Silverlight) may be required to run the web application.
On-premise database deployments must run on Oracle 19C.

No Personal Identifiable Information (PII) may be stored in any database table unless the application has a specific business need for that data.

All web applications must adhere to the W3 Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 at 'AA' level of conformance (WCAG 2.1 AA).

component_records.title: Bid administration and RFP schedule compliance
component_records.description: A bid manager owns the proposal calendar and the RFP's own procedural obligations: the proposal is filed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by the stated deadline with time treated as of the essence, and every RFP event the Offeror attends or triggers is scheduled inside the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window. All questions and comments are submitted in writing to the RFP mailbox no later than 17 July 2024 at 4 p.m. Central, with no contact with MoDOT employees by any other route, and the team diaries the 31 July 2024 response posting and the 18 September 2024 selection notification. The same calendar discipline carries into the contract, where the fixed milestone dates are tracked as binding.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the engagement on a 15-month baseline with a kick-off meeting to review work plan, scope and schedule and to set the communication protocol, quarterly status meetings with written minutes, and monthly e-mail and phone progress updates to the MoDOT project manager. The work plan details task implementation, resources and schedule, and is submitted for MoDOT approval with MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans expressly recognised. All activity is coordinated with the Construction and Materials Division and with MHTC's designated representative, and advice and information are made available as the work progresses. A single point of contact handles all consultation on administration concerns.

component_records.title: Reporting, deliverables and publication compliance
component_records.description: A reporting calendar delivers quarterly progress reports on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December, an interim presentation near the project mid-point, and the full deliverable set: final report with a completed Technical Report Documentation page, a 1-2 page research summary, a staff presentation, and the user manual. All documents follow the Publication Guidelines and summary template, and the draft final report, summary and manual are submitted on 3 November 2025 with final documents on 1 January 2026 and the final invoice on 2 February 2026. Nothing is released publicly without MHTC's representative's prior consent.

component_records.title: Data Management Plan and data stewardship
component_records.description: A Data Management Plan is delivered within two weeks of kick-off (target 4 December 2024) describing the anticipated formats of all data and related files, committing to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the corpus, annotations and outputs remain usable after the contract. The plan also sets retention, access and handover arrangements consistent with MHTC ownership of all deliverables and information supplied to the Offeror, and with records being available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor for three years after final payment.

component_records.title: Literature review and state-of-practice benchmarking
component_records.description: A structured review of published research and other state DOT practice in applying AI/ML to right-of-way work, covering deed and metes-and-bounds description generation, document automation and survey-data workflows, with a documented search protocol, inclusion criteria and a comparison matrix of practices, tools and reported outcomes. Findings feed directly into the program selection and the proof-of-concept design, and are reported as a standalone deliverable and summarised in the final report.

component_records.title: Requirements baseline: EPG 236.4.6.2 and MHTC parameters
component_records.description: Before any drafting logic is built, the team codifies the description rules into a written requirements baseline: MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2, the metes-and-bounds convention for all realty rights acquired or conveyed, and the rule that a property acquired in its entirety is described exactly as it appears on the last deed of record. The baseline defines the MHTC parameters the AI/ML draft must use, including the deed-of-record lookup and the entirety-versus-partial decision, and is reviewed and signed off by a Missouri professional land surveyor against right of way plans. This baseline is the acceptance reference for every generated draft.

component_records.title: LLD drafting program selection and IS approval
component_records.description: The team names the specific program used to develop LLDs and submits it to MoDOT Information Systems for approval before any Task 3c proof-of-concept work begins, including version, licensing, hosting model, data flows and security documentation. The selection is constrained to approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or .NET Framework 4.8+) with MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, in C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML or Python, with no third-party tool that places a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior BRPT and IS management approval. Python use is limited to small one-time scripts unless BRPT approves larger use. A contingency plan holds the build at the approval gate so a delayed approval does not consume the schedule.

component_records.title: Web-based LLD drafting application and proof of concept
component_records.description: A browser-based application, with no client-side software beyond a modern browser, that ingests right of way plans and deed data and generates a first draft legal land description for ROW staff to review and edit. It runs on Oracle 19C on-premise (or the latest supported SQL Server where MoDOT IS Data Service Management approves), stores no PII without a documented business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval, meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri accessibility standard, carries no vendor branding where a licensed option removes it, and uses only properly licensed third-party content. Library dependencies are reviewed annually and the application is tested against the latest IS-approved browsers. The proof of concept demonstrates drafts across a variety of property types, with MoDOT reviewing each draft and feeding improvements back into the model and rules.

component_records.title: Demonstration, training and user manual
component_records.description: A live demonstration on 25 April 2025 shows how the AI/ML creates draft LLDs, followed by MoDOT review and improvement cycles. Once the system is finalised, ROW staff training is delivered by 25 July 2025 in a mix of instructor-led sessions (on-site and virtual) and recorded walkthroughs, supported by a user manual covering end-user drafting, review and edit workflows plus administration. Training materials and the manual are handed over as editable source files so MoDOT can re-run sessions for new staff after the contract ends.

component_records.title: Cost estimate and price page
component_records.description: A completed, signed Section (4) Price Page and cost estimate covering every service in the Scope of Work, broken down into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration Cost, Miscellaneous and Total, with miscellaneous items itemised on an attached sheet. The estimate is built bottom-up from the work plan by task and by month across the full 15-month term, totals no more than $175,000, and is offered as a firm price under the RFP terms. A priced contingency line covers the IS approval gate and additional MoDOT review cycles.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A compliance lead accepts and administers the RFP's contractual terms: the post-award negotiated contract provisions, MHTC's right to cancel the award if terms cannot be agreed, no assignment or delegation without written consent, MHTC's written clarifications governing over conflicting terms, and formal amendment for any change. The component carries Missouri Executive Order 07-13 compliance, E-Verify MOU documentation, sworn affidavits of non-disemployment and lawful presence, flow-down of Section (3) paragraph I to every subcontract with Commission-directed enforcement, and prime responsibility for subcontractor quality. It also holds General Liability at $500,000 per person / $3,000,000 per occurrence, Automobile Liability at the same limits, Missouri Workers' Compensation, confidential-information handling with immediate notification of any disclosure request, and records retention for three years after final payment. Minority and women hiring and 10% MBE / 5% WBE participation are pursued and reported.

items.text: Fixed 2 February 2026 end date conflicts with the 15-month term. The RFP states a 15-month contract period but also fixes the contract end and final invoice at 2 February 2026. If the award or contract execution slips past early November 2024, the 15-month term and the fixed end date cannot both hold, and the bidder either compresses the work or absorbs uncompensated effort. The proposed solution treats both as binding, which leaves no room to reconcile them. R016 and R041 are directly contradictory, and the RFP's own schedule (selection 18 September 2024, presumed 1 November 2024 start) leaves almost no float for contract negotiation before the 15-month clock and the fixed end date diverge.
items.reason: 15-month term and 2/2/2026 end date are stated, but 'presumed 1 November 2024 start' and contract slippage are not in sources; 'directly contradictory' overstated.

items.text: Referenced exhibits and forms are missing from the RFP. Missing or wrongly formatted affidavits and pricing pages are a stated cause for disqualification, so the bid can be lost on paperwork rather than merit. The RFP makes submission of the required data sufficient cause for disqualification (R071) and requires the signed Price Page (R093), yet the exhibits and forms are absent from the PDF and must be obtained from MoDOT's website.
items.reason: Exhibit A/B page 15 reference, missing forms and PDF absence are not in sources; also R071 misquoted as making submission cause for disqualification.

items.text: IS approval of the named LLD program gates the whole build. The Offeror must name the LLD development program and obtain MoDOT Information Systems approval before Task 3c can start, but the RFP does not say what documentation is needed or how long approval takes. A slow or conditional approval pushes the 25 April 2025 demonstration and every later milestone, and the fixed end date does not move. Approval is a hard gate on the critical path (R053) with an undefined process and turnaround, and the demonstration date is fixed only about five months after the presumed start.
items.reason: Name and IS approval before Task 3c and 4/25/2025 date supported; 'presumed start', 'five months', and approval process being undefined unsupported.

items.text: EPG 236.4.6.2 and the MHTC parameters are not supplied. The drafting rules the AI must follow live in MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 and in undefined 'MHTC parameters', neither of which is in the RFP. If the guide is revised, internally inconsistent or unavailable, the requirements baseline and the acceptance reference for every generated draft shift after the price is fixed, forcing rework of the rules engine and the training data. R012 and R015 depend on a document the RFP does not include and a parameter set it does not define, and the solution's own assumption is that the guide is obtainable and stable for the term.
items.reason: EPG section and MHTC parameters cited, but that they are not supplied or undefined, and rules-engine consequences, are not in sources.

items.text: $175,000 cap may be below the cost of the full scope. The engagement is a firm, not-to-exceed $175,000 covering a literature review, a named and IS-approved program, a working proof of concept across multiple property types, ROW staff training, a user manual, and draft and final reports over 15 months. The RFP does not define the number of demonstration properties, training volume or review cycles, so the scope can grow while the price cannot. The bidder either under-prices and loses money or trims scope and scores poorly. The cap is fixed (R042) while the effort drivers (property count, training size, review rounds) are explicitly left open, and the solution's own assumptions size them to fit the cap rather than to the RFP.
items.reason: $175,000 not-to-exceed and cost estimate requirements supported; 'firm', scope list, 15 months, and undefined property counts or review cycles not in sources.

items.text: Oracle 19C and SQL Server requirements conflict. One requirement mandates Oracle 19C for on-premise databases while another directs the application to run on the latest supported SQL Server, with 2016+ allowed on approval. Building and licensing for both platforms doubles the database work and the licence cost inside a $175,000 cap; picking one risks rejection at IS review. R142 and R143 are contradictory as written, and the proposed solution hedges by offering SQL Server only with IS approval, which leaves the platform undecided at pricing time.
items.reason: Oracle 19C and SQL Server (latest, 2016+ with approval) requirements are stated in cited sources; conflict and cost consequences are judgment.

items.text: Demonstration, training and manual scope is undefined. The RFP fixes the dates for the 25 April 2025 demonstration and the 25 July 2025 training but not the number or types of properties, the audience size, the number of sessions or the depth of the user manual. The bidder cannot size the effort reliably, and MoDOT may expect more than was priced, particularly if training is expected to be repeated for new staff. R054, R055 and R056 carry no volume or format, and the solution assumes a modest property set and a single training cohort without confirmation.
items.reason: Dates and tasks are supported, but absence of property counts, audience size, sessions, and manual depth cannot be verified from the cited sources.

items.text: Unreadable pages 19 and 20 may hide task or deliverable requirements. Pages 19 and 20 carry only 19 words each and are dominated by images, so the task descriptions for project management and the literature review may be incomplete in the text the team can read. If those pages contain deliverable formats, acceptance criteria or task detail, the proposal and the price may omit required work. Two consecutive pages in the middle of the task section are effectively unreadable, and the solution's work plan for Tasks 1 and 2 rests on partial text; the impact depends on what the images actually contain.
items.reason: Cited sources say nothing about pages 19-20 being unreadable, image-dominated, or having 19 words each.

items.text: Fixed milestone dates may be re-opened at kick-off. The RFP fixes the demonstration, training, interim presentation, draft and final document dates, yet also says key milestone dates will be determined at the kick-off meeting. If MoDOT moves them after award, the schedule the bidder priced and staffed no longer holds, and the small consortium may not have the people available at the new dates. The milestone table and the kick-off row contradict each other, and the solution assumes the fixed dates are binding, which is a reasonable but unconfirmed reading.
items.reason: Table fixes milestone dates while kick-off row says key milestone dates determined at meeting; tension is stated in sources.

items.text: Accessibility and PII obligations may need unplanned remediation. The application must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri accessibility standard, and may store no PII without a documented business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval. Deed and right of way records routinely contain names and parcel owner details, so the no-PII design may conflict with the data the model needs, and accessibility conformance is untested until late in a short build. R144, R145 and R147 are mandatory, the accessibility standard is only linked rather than reproduced, and the solution assumes no PII is stored without confirming what the deed corpus contains.
items.reason: WCAG, state standard link, PII restrictions and approval are all in sources; deed-data concerns are risk judgment.

items.text: Insurance limits and contract terms may not be acceptable as written. The RFP requires General and Automobile Liability at $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, Missouri Workers' Compensation, E-Verify documentation and sworn affidavits, and lets MHTC cancel the award if post-award terms cannot be agreed. A small research consortium may not carry those limits or may find the negotiated terms unacceptable after spending bid effort. R126, R127 and R128 are firm requirements while the RFP introduces insurance as something the Offeror 'may be asked' about, and R098 allows MHTC to cancel the award on failed negotiation.
items.reason: Insurance limits, workers' comp, E-Verify, affidavits, 'may be asked' wording and cancellation right are all in the cited sources.

items.text: Monthly updates and quarterly status meetings are set against each other. One requirement demands monthly e-mail and phone progress updates, another quarterly status meetings with written minutes. The proposed solution treats them as cumulative, which is the safe reading but adds meeting, minute-writing and reporting effort that must be absorbed inside the fixed cap and the small consortium's staffing. R032 and R045 conflict on reporting cadence, and the solution's assumption that both apply is reasonable but adds recurring effort across 15 months.
items.reason: Monthly updates and quarterly meetings are supported; '15 months' duration and fixed cap are not in cited sources.
